stem: The branch of biology concerned with identification, nomenclature and classification of organisms is_____
solution: Taxonomy is the branch of biology that deals with the identification, nomenclature and classification of organisms. Ecology studies the interaction of organisms with their environment, physiology studies function, and anatomy studies internal structure. Matches option B.

stem: Systematics differs from taxonomy mainly because systematics also considers:
solution: Taxonomy classifies and names organisms. Systematics does that and also studies the diversity of organisms and the evolutionary (phylogenetic) relationships among them, so it goes beyond external morphology, habitat or economic use. Matches option B.

stem: The basic unit of classification is:
solution: Species is the basic and lowest unit of classification, defined as a group of organisms capable of interbreeding. Genus, family and order are progressively higher categories. Matches option C.

stem: Which sequence represents the taxonomic hierarchy from higher to lower category?
optA: Kingdom → Phylum → Class → Order → Family → Genus → Species
optB: Kingdom → Class → Phylum → Order → Family → Species → Genus
optC: Species → Genus → Family → Order → Class → Phylum → Kingdom
optD: Kingdom → Order → Class → Phylum → Family → Genus → Species
solution: The taxonomic hierarchy from higher to lower is Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species. Option B swaps Phylum and Class and ends with Genus, option C is the reverse (lower to higher) order, and option D misplaces Order and Class. Matches option A.

stem: In binomial nomenclature, the first word of a scientific name represents the:
solution: In binomial nomenclature a scientific name has two words: the first is the generic name (the genus), the second is the specific epithet. Matches option B.

stem: Who proposed the five-kingdom classification system in 1969?
solution: R.H. Whittaker proposed the five-kingdom classification (Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, Animalia) in 1969. Linnaeus gave the earlier two-kingdom system and Haeckel had proposed a three-kingdom scheme. Matches option B.

stem: Which of the following is NOT a major criterion used by Whittaker in five-kingdom classification?
solution: Whittaker's criteria were cell structure, thallus organisation, mode of nutrition, mode of reproduction and phylogenetic relationships. Blood group applies only to some animals and cannot be a criterion for classifying all organisms. Matches option D.

stem: A taxonomic category containing related genera is called:
solution: A family is a taxonomic category made up of related genera, just as an order is made up of related families. Matches option B.

stem: The scientific name of an organism is generally written using:
solution: Scientific names are written using the binomial system introduced by Linnaeus, in which each name has a generic name and a specific epithet. Matches option B.

stem: Which taxonomic category is immediately above species?
solution: Species is the lowest taxonomic category and genus is the category immediately above it, containing a group of related species. Matches option B.

stem: Which kingdom contains prokaryotic organisms?
solution: Kingdom Monera contains all the prokaryotes, that is bacteria, cyanobacteria, archaebacteria and mycoplasma. Protista, Fungi and Plantae are all eukaryotic kingdoms. Matches option C.

stem: A characteristic feature of Monera is the absence of:
solution: Monerans are prokaryotes, so their genetic material is not enclosed by a nuclear membrane. They do possess a cell membrane, ribosomes and DNA, so those options are wrong. Matches option C.

stem: The genetic material of most bacteria is present in the:
solution: In a bacterial cell the DNA lies free in the cytoplasm in a region called the nucleoid, which has no bounding membrane. A nucleolus, mitochondrion and chloroplast are all eukaryotic structures. Matches option B.

stem: The cell wall of most eubacteria is primarily composed of:
solution: The eubacterial cell wall is built mainly of peptidoglycan, also called murein. Chitin is the fungal wall material, while cellulose and pectin belong to plant cell walls. Matches option C.

stem: Which group of bacteria is well known for living in extreme environments?
solution: Archaebacteria live in the most extreme habitats: halophiles in very salty water, thermoacidophiles in hot springs, and methanogens in marshy areas. Their distinctive cell wall lets them survive there. Matches option B.

stem: Methanogens are commonly found in:
solution: Methanogens occur in marshy areas and in the rumen (stomach) of cattle, where they act on cellulose in the dung and produce methane gas. Matches option B.

stem: Which of the following is a cyanobacterium?
solution: Nostoc is a filamentous cyanobacterium, that is a member of Monera. Agaricus (mushroom) and Rhizopus (bread mould) are fungi, and Amoeba is a protozoan. Matches option A.

stem: Nitrogen fixation in some cyanobacteria is associated with specialized cells called:
solution: In filamentous cyanobacteria such as Nostoc and Anabaena, nitrogen fixation takes place in specialised thick-walled cells called heterocysts. Conidia and basidia are fungal spore structures and zoospores are motile spores. Matches option B.

stem: Which organism lacks a cell wall and is considered among the smallest free-living organisms?
solution: Mycoplasma completely lacks a cell wall and is the smallest known free-living organism; it can survive without oxygen. Nostoc, E. coli and Rhizobium all possess cell walls. Matches option A.

stem: The organisms responsible for curdling milk include:
solution: Lactic acid bacteria such as Lactobacillus convert the milk sugar lactose into lactic acid, which curdles milk into curd. Plasmodium and Amoeba are protozoans and Penicillium is a fungus. Matches option A.

stem: Which of the following kingdoms has/have only unicellular organisms?
solution: In the five-kingdom scheme, Monera and Protista are the two kingdoms treated as wholly unicellular, while Fungi, Plantae and Animalia are predominantly multicellular. Matches option C. [Note: some monerans, such as the filamentous cyanobacterium Nostoc, grow as filaments or colonies, but these are aggregates of independent cells and not a truly multicellular body, so the kingdom is still classed as unicellular.]
reviewNote: Exact duplicate of NDA II 2018 PYQ already in the bank (19496b5c) - same stem, same four options, same key C. The printed paper's '[PYQ - NDA II 2018]' annotation has been stripped from the stem.

stem: Archaebacteria differ from eubacteria chiefly in the composition of their:
solution: Archaebacteria differ from eubacteria chiefly in the chemistry of the cell wall, which lacks peptidoglycan and is built instead of pseudomurein or protein. This distinctive wall is what allows them to live in extreme habitats. Matches option A.

stem: Which bacterial group is primarily photosynthetic and commonly called blue-green algae?
solution: Cyanobacteria are photosynthetic prokaryotes containing chlorophyll a, and because of their pigments they are commonly called blue-green algae. Matches option A.

stem: The bacterial cell wall generally provides:
solution: The rigid bacterial cell wall determines the shape of the cell and protects it from bursting in a dilute medium. Protein synthesis is carried out by ribosomes and ATP synthesis by the cell membrane and mesosome. Matches option B.

stem: Which one of the following is NOT a prokaryotic feature?
solution: Prokaryotes have 70S ribosomes, a nucleoid in place of a nucleus, and divide by binary fission. A membrane-bound nucleus is the defining eukaryotic feature and is absent in prokaryotes. Matches option B.

stem: Kingdom Protista mainly includes:
solution: Kingdom Protista is made up of single-celled eukaryotes and forms a link between the prokaryotic Monera and the multicellular eukaryotic kingdoms. Matches option A.

stem: Diatoms are included in the group:
solution: Chrysophytes is the group that includes the diatoms together with the golden algae (desmids). Euglenoids, dinoflagellates and slime moulds are separate protistan groups. Matches option A.

stem: The cell wall of diatoms is mainly composed of:
solution: The diatom cell wall forms two thin overlapping halves, the frustule, whose walls are embedded with silica. This makes them indestructible, and their piled-up remains form diatomaceous earth. Matches option B.

stem: Which group of protists is characterized by two flagella and often causes red tides?
solution: Dinoflagellates bear two flagella and, when they multiply rapidly in the sea, they colour the water and cause red tides. Matches option A.

stem: Euglena is best described as:
solution: Euglena photosynthesises when sunlight is available but feeds heterotrophically on smaller organisms in the dark, so its nutrition is mixotrophic. Matches option C.

stem: The pellicle in Euglena mainly helps in:
solution: In place of a cell wall Euglena has a protein-rich layer called the pellicle, which keeps the body flexible while still maintaining its shape. Matches option B.

stem: Slime moulds are generally:
solution: Slime moulds are saprophytic protists. Their body moves as a plasmodium over decaying matter and, under unfavourable conditions, forms fruiting bodies bearing spores. Matches option B.

stem: Amoeba belongs to:
solution: Amoeba belongs to the protozoans, in the amoeboid group, and moves and captures its food using pseudopodia. Matches option A.

stem: Which protist is known for a silica-rich cell covering?
solution: The diatom is the protist whose cell wall is impregnated with silica, forming the two-piece frustule. Amoeba, Paramecium and Plasmodium have no such silica covering. Matches option A.
reviewNote: Duplicates Q28 of this same paper (diatom / silica, asked in reverse). Kept for paper fidelity; only Q28 should reach the public bank.

stem: Which of the following is an important ecological role of diatoms?
optA: Major primary producers in aquatic ecosystems
solution: Diatoms are the chief primary producers in the oceans and account for a large share of aquatic photosynthesis. Nitrogen fixation in roots is done by bacteria, wood decay by fungi, and antibiotics come from fungi and actinomycetes. Matches option A.

stem: Kingdom Fungi is characterized by:
solution: Fungi are eukaryotes with a definite nucleus, and because they lack chlorophyll they are heterotrophic, living as saprophytes, parasites or symbionts. Matches option B.

stem: The fungal cell wall is mainly made up of:
solution: The fungal cell wall is made of chitin along with polysaccharides, which distinguishes it from the cellulose wall of plants and the peptidoglycan wall of bacteria. Matches option B.

stem: The reserve food material in fungi is mainly:
solution: Fungi store their reserve food as glycogen and oil droplets. Starch is the storage material of plants, so it is not the fungal reserve. Matches option B.

stem: The thread-like structures forming the body of most fungi are called:
solution: The body of most fungi is made of long, thread-like filaments called hyphae. Rhizoids are anchoring structures, stolons are only one kind of hypha, and flagella are organs of movement. Matches option A.

stem: A mass of interconnected fungal hyphae is called:
solution: A network of many interwoven and interconnected hyphae is called a mycelium. Matches option A.

stem: Yeast is a:
solution: Yeast is a single-celled (unicellular) fungus, widely used in baking and in brewing. Matches option A.

stem: Asexual reproduction in yeast commonly occurs by:
solution: Yeast reproduces asexually mainly by budding, in which a small outgrowth forms on the parent cell, enlarges and then separates. Matches option B.

stem: Which fungal group is commonly called sac fungi?
solution: Ascomycetes are called sac fungi because their sexual spores, the ascospores, are produced inside a sac-like structure called the ascus. Matches option B.

stem: Mushrooms and puffballs are commonly associated with:
solution: Mushrooms, bracket fungi and puffballs all belong to the Basidiomycetes. Matches option A.

stem: Which structure produces basidiospores in basidiomycetes?
solution: In basidiomycetes the basidiospores are produced on the outside of a club-shaped structure called the basidium. An ascocarp belongs to ascomycetes, a sporangium to phycomycetes, and a conidiophore bears conidia. Matches option A.

stem: Lichens represent a symbiotic association between:
solution: A lichen is a symbiotic association between a fungus and either an alga or a cyanobacterium. The fungus gives shelter and absorbs mineral nutrients and water, while the photosynthetic partner prepares food. Matches option A.

stem: Lichens are useful as indicators of:
solution: Lichens are very sensitive to sulphur dioxide and simply do not grow where the air is polluted, so their presence or absence is used as an indicator of air pollution. Matches option A.
reviewNote: Measured p = 0.03 (3 of 90 students). Key A is unambiguously correct and both blind passes rated it HIGH, but the whole cohort avoided it - 49 chose 'soil salinity only' and 34 'water hardness'. Flagged to the school as a teaching or answer-sheet anomaly; the key is not in doubt.

stem: Which one of the following statements about fungi is NOT correct?
optC: They store food mainly as starch
solution: Fungi are heterotrophic, their cell wall contains chitin, and many of them reproduce by spores, so those three statements are correct. They store food as glycogen and oils rather than starch, so that statement is not correct. Matches option C.

stem: Which of the following is correctly matched?
solution: Rhizopus is the common bread mould, so this pair is correctly matched. Amoeba is a protozoan and not a fungus, Nostoc is a cyanobacterium and not a basidiomycete, and Euglena is a protistan flagellate and not a cyanobacterium. Matches option A.

stem: Which one of the following correctly represents the order of increasing taxonomic rank?
solution: Arranged in increasing order of rank, species is the lowest, then genus, then family, then order. Matches option A.
